optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions

professionalSummary.text: Senior product analyst with two years of experience on a subscription product team, specializing in translating subscription operations and customer success intake into user stories with acceptance criteria for self‑service billing and seat‑management pages.
professionalSummary.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self‑service billing pages.

experienceHighlights.text: Turned weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for seat‑change and invoice‑download pages, each story carrying acceptance criteria.
experienceHighlights.witness: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self‑service seat‑change and invoice‑download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.

experienceHighlights.text: Led acceptance sessions for three billing‑page releases, logging every criterion as passed or failed.
experienceHighlights.witness: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

experienceHighlights.text: Agreed release scope with engineering and subscription operations during sprint planning, maintaining a record of decisions.
experienceHighlights.witness: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

experienceHighlights.text: Published release notes for seat‑change and invoice‑download pages, detailing limitations and support hand‑over requirements.
experienceHighlights.witness: Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Work sample: story set for the invoice‑download page with acceptance criteria and pass/fail log from an acceptance session, including ticket identifiers for traceability.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the story set for the invoice-download page with its acceptance criteria, plus the pass/fail log from one acceptance session; ticket identifiers are included so the entries can be traced.

skills.witness: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self‑service seat‑change and invoice‑download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.
Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.
Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work sample documents establish the candidate’s experience in user story creation, acceptance session facilitation, release scope coordination, and release notes authoring for subscription‑based self‑service billing pages. They do not provide documented evidence that the delivered features reduced billing support tickets against a monthly baseline.

Human review should focus on obtaining and verifying ticket volume data and attribution analysis.
